open_notes: Every quota fact is adopted from the General Reference table (it has the Adjustable column). The guide quota page (quota-limits) and the General Reference disagree on one description: Nodes per Region applies to non-reserved nodes only (guide) versus reserved and non-reserved nodes (General Reference). The fact keeps to the number 300 and adjustable, which both pages share.
The 15 similarity conflicts that the quota template claims opened were closed with --both (different quotas). Conflicts cf-1009 to cf-1011 belong to the behavior lens.

Minimum metered storage: the guide page WhatIs.corecomponents says 1 GB without naming an engine; the pricing page and the FAQ say 100 MB for Valkey and 1 GB for Memcached and Redis OSS. The pricing page is used (fact elasticache-serverless-minimum-metered-storage).

Serverless supported versions: the guide deployment table says Memcached 1.6.22 and higher (WhatIs also says 1.6.22); the FAQ says Memcached 1.4.5 and above. The guide is current truth; the FAQ wording is recorded in the note of elasticache-serverless-vs-node-based-supported-versions.

Shards page versus NodeGroups page: the engine condition for the 500-node limit differs (Valkey 7.2 and higher or Redis OSS 5.0.6 to 7.1, versus Valkey or Redis OSS 5.0.6 or higher). The Shards page is used. The quota page default (90 nodes per cluster, adjustable) and the 500 maximum agree.

Change facts have no old value except two: the Multi-AZ SLA of ElastiCache for Redis (99.9% to 99.99%, What's New post 2023-01-31) and Memcached snapshots (customers could not back up Memcached workloads, post 2024-06-12). History rows and What's New posts of the other changes do not state an old value verbatim, so changed is null and volatility is frequently-changing (mechanical check M9 forbids changed-since-2022 without a changed object).

What's New pages for 2024/06, 2024/05, 2023/01 and others are blocked by robots.txt; those changes are cited from the one-line API snapshot (api/whats-new-v2-amazon-elasticache-s1000-p0). A quote from that snapshot must start and end at an inner sentence boundary, so first and last sentences of a post could not be quoted; the change date then sits in the note and in change_items, not in the claim.

d001.note: All four are adjustable except nodes per shard (6, not adjustable).

d003.note: Default 90 nodes per cluster (90 shards with 0 replicas to 15 shards with 5 replicas), raisable to 500; 5 replicas per shard is the maximum. Pages agree.

d004.note: Cluster mode disabled: 1 shard, 0 to 5 read replicas.

d010.note: AWS says microsecond latency for ElastiCache, sub-millisecond for a remote cache, double-digit milliseconds at best for a disk-based database. The whitepaper sentence on remote caches is a historical-reference whitepaper; the behavior lens has elasticache-cache-types-remote-cache-submillisecond-latency.
